result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.simrank_star_similarity_pair()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute SimRank* similarity between a specific pair of nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L20886-L21002){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.simrank_star_similarity_pair( source, target, importance_factor=0.8, max_iterations=100, tolerance=1e-06, method="closed_form", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![SimRank* similarity for one pair](/assets/graphs/simrank-star-similarity-pair.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Nodes B and E are outlined in the accent color; the short paths between them through C and D are in accent. SimRank* counts paths of every length, decayed by the factor C = 0.8 per step, and the card returns a score of 0.297 for the pair." width="100%"} Returns the SimRank* similarity of `source` and `target` as a single float, using the same definition and solvers as `simrank_star_similarity()`. SimRank* considers paths of every length between the two nodes, discounted by `importance_factor=` per step, so nodes that are close together or share neighbors score high and distant nodes score low. The result is symmetric, and a node's similarity with itself is `1.0`. The graph is not modified. This is a convenience for when only one score is needed, e.g., checking how similar two specific products, accounts, or pages are. It is *not* cheaper than the all-pairs method: internally the full `n x n` similarity matrix is still solved (*O(n³)* time, *O(n²)* memory) and one entry is returned. When scoring many pairs, call `simrank_star_similarity(return_dict=True)` once and look the pairs up instead. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The first node of the pair, given as a node ID (`int`) or label (`str`). [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The second node of the pair, given as a node ID (`int`) or label (`str`). Since the score is symmetric, swapping `source` and `target` gives the same result. If it is the same node as `source`, `1.0` is returned immediately. [importance_factor]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.8]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Decay factor `C`, which must be in `[0, 1)`. Higher values let similarity propagate along longer paths and raise scores; lower values make the score depend mostly on immediate neighborhoods. Default is `0.8`. [max_iterations]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of fixed-point iterations for `method="iterative"`. Too few iterations underestimates (or misses) similarity between nodes linked only by longer paths. Ignored by `"closed_form"`. Default is `100`. [tolerance]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence threshold for `method="iterative"`: iteration stops early once the overall change in the similarity matrix between two iterations falls below this value. Ignored by `"closed_form"`. Default is `1e-6`. [method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["closed_form"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Solver to use. `"closed_form"` (default) solves the PJsim Lyapunov equation exactly via Bartels-Stewart. `"iterative"` uses fixed-point iteration controlled by `max_iterations=` and `tolerance=`, and converges to the same value. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Similarity score in `[0, 1]`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If either node does not exist, if `importance_factor=` is outside `[0, 1)`, or if `method=` is not `"closed_form"` or `"iterative"`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} `A` and `B` are linked to the same two nodes (`C` and `D`), while `E` hangs off `C`. Under the default settings `A` is noticeably more similar to `B` than to `E`: ::: {#5935c48e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) graph.add_edges([("A", "C"), ("A", "D"), ("B", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "E")]) ( round(graph.simrank_star_similarity_pair("A", "B"), 3), round(graph.simrank_star_similarity_pair("A", "E"), 3), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (0.443, 0.394) ``` ::: ::: The iterative solver converges to the same score as the closed form. With `max_iterations=1`, however, it has not yet followed any path from `A` to `B` and still reports `0.0`: ::: {#9055a4d4 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} [ round(graph.simrank_star_similarity_pair("A", "B", method="iterative"), 3), graph.simrank_star_similarity_pair("A", "B", method="iterative", max_iterations=1), ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [0.443, 0.0] ``` ::: ::: Raising `importance_factor=` lets similarity accumulate over longer paths, so the score grows: ::: {#30021038 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} [ round(graph.simrank_star_similarity_pair("A", "B", importance_factor=c), 3) for c in [0.5, 0.8, 0.95] ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [0.131, 0.443, 0.804] ``` ::: :::
